title: Aeoniums and Dyckia 'Cactus Ranch Red'
description: Dyckia bromeliads can add a lot of excitement in a garden, especially when given strong contrast.  The thin spikes of bright orange flowers in summer almost appear to dance in the wind.  The foliage can be almot black, a perfect match for Aeonium 'Swartzkop'.  The shiny green Aeoniums are a perfect foil.

title: View of garden from lower bathroom window
Stairs up to terrace off family room
Near continuous color for a planter
description: The plantings were chosen to combine some cooler, soothing pastel lavenders, soft pinkish grays and purples with deep reds, offset by the apricot orange new growth of the Banksia blechnifolia.  I wanted this planter to be colorful 12 months of the year, including January when the house was first opened to the public.  None of these plants would have performed as seen in the dead of winter if not for the full sun exposure and perfect drainage offered by being 3 stories up in the air.  It does help to know what effects you are after, and know how the plants will perform in the environment where they are placed.

title: Stairs from upper terrace down to jacuzzi
Heliconia schiedeana's at jacuzzi
description: The plants are probably a little over the top in this photo, with the Angelica pachycarpa threatening to take over the jacuzzi, and Heliconia's thick enough to harbor some slithering snakes.  In fact, it is simply the end of spring and the beginning of summer in this Berkeley hills garden.  There's only one thing blooming in this photo, but still plenty of interest from foliage form and texture.

description: These are built-in planters with plumbed in drainage system and automatic drip irrigation system, floating about 8 feet above the sloping ground below.

title: Dyckia 'Cactus Ranch Red' in bloom
description: The planting design is almost Mondrian in layout, with contrasting blocks of colors and textures.  I particularly like how the pale green play off the darker tones, in sort of a back and forth rhythym.

title: 28 Vallejo St Rear Terrace Planter off kitchen
description: Graptoveria 'Fred Ives' with Anigozanthus  and Banksia blechniifolia in raised built-in planter at deck off kitchen.  This Banksia has marvelous foliage that resemble a Blechnum fern, thereby the species name, and also sends out fuzzy creeping rhizomes that will drape over the wall or cover the ground, and form large colonies of stiff foliage with the occasional bizarre Banksia cone-like flowers.  The succulent Graptoveria also forms large clumps which will further drape over the wall with age, mingling with the Banksia in time.

title: Far corner of garden with concrete bench-wall
Large Vietnamese stone pots with Cannomois grande
Trachycarpus fortunei, Angelica pachycarpa and Mahonia lomariifolia
Aechmea pineliana v. minuta and Sedum palmeri
description: This has always been one of my favorite smaller growing Aechmea's for use in the garden.  It looks as good all by itself in a pot as it does in a garden setting.  With sufficient sun it will turn very bright rosy purple, and the flowering spikes are attractive for months at a time.  I just wish it grew faster for me, it is very slow under cool summer conditions.  I also find this one is very slow to grow roots, and can't take drying out too long or the foliage starts to die off.

title: View of stairs from downstairs bathroom window
View out lower bedroom window to front courtyard
description: This shot is taken through the window of the lower level bedroom, and shows how the pots are used to frame the view against the wall, without cutting off daylight.  A selection of plants of predominant green and greenish blue hues are used, such as the Sedum palmeri draping the pot below the Asplenium bulbiferum fern, looking across to the variegated Clerodendrum trichotomum 'Harlequin' against the wall. The palm fronds are a glimpse of Chamaedorea costaricana in a container, which absolutely loved being up against this north facing wall.   I love how the stripped trunk of the Windmill Palm picks up some of the same blues and greens.

title: View across lower garden back to jacuzzi
Clematis x 'Avalanche' foliage at wall
description: A detail photo of the shiny cut-leaf foliage of this evergreen Clematis, a hybrid of two New Zealand species, paniculata x marmoraria.  It makes incredibly sculptural pendant lines of foliage, best shown against a contrasting wall, such as the white stucco  here.

title: Color for the sun
description: The combination of Linaria reticulata and the Alyogyne huegelli were both selected for this planter off the kitchen cantilevered deck for their nonstop continuous bloom, winter/spring/summer/fall.  The Linaria is a great annual for color at any time of year, and can be counted on to bloom heavily about 6 weeks after being planted out.  One of my tricks for getting this to bloom this massively, is to cut off all flower buds at least twice about 2 weeks apart before I finally let it bloom.  If not for this step, it is often a rather wispy thing, with a lot less presence.  The Blue Hibiscus, Alyogyne, requires regular dead heading and tip pinching to maintain best appearance in a close-up planter such as this, but can reward with almost continual year round bloom.  This planter also has some draping plants such as Banksia blechnifolia and Petrea volubilis which were intended to give another dimension of vivid flowering color as they draped down over the wall.
